title: Induction Generator Communication Fault
shortDescription: The touch control board has lost communication with the induction generator module.
fullDescription:
Electrolux induction cooktops use a touch control PCB that talks to the power generator board over a ribbon cable or serial bus. When that link drops, the cooktop displays E1 and disables heating on all zones.

Common triggers are a loose ribbon connector after service, moisture ingress, or a failed filter capacitor on the generator board. Restoring the connection or replacing the generator usually clears the fault.

causes.cause: Loose ribbon cable between touch board and generator

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off at the breaker for 5 minutes and restore power.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the cooktop and reseat the ribbon cable between control and generator boards.

fixSteps.title: Replace generator
fixSteps.instruction: If fault persists, swap the induction generator module.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the generator needs replacement or you are uncomfortable under mains voltage.

faq.q: Can I still use the cooktop with E1?
faq.a: No, all zones are disabled until the communication fault is cleared.

title: Cooktop Overheating
shortDescription: Internal temperature of the induction module has exceeded safe limits.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the NTC sensor on the generator heat sink has detected excessive temperature. The unit halts heating until it cools down.

Causes include blocked cooling airflow beneath the cooktop, failed cooling fan, or prolonged use of very high power settings in a hot ambient environment.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off and let the cooktop cool for 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the cabinet ventilation gap below the cooktop is unobstructed.

fixSteps.title: Check fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the cooling fan spins freely and replace if seized.

whenToCallPro: If fan is fine and E2 returns, the generator NTC or board needs professional diagnosis.

faq.a: It is a protective shutdown, not immediately dangerous, but should be resolved before continued use.

title: Unsuitable or Missing Cookware
shortDescription: The induction zone cannot detect a ferromagnetic pan.
fullDescription:
Induction zones require cookware with a magnetic base. E3 appears when the pan is non-ferromagnetic, too small, off-centre, or missing.

Test by touching a magnet to the pan base. If it does not stick, the pan is incompatible with induction.

causes.cause: Pan smaller than minimum zone diameter

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: Check pan base with a magnet; replace if not magnetic.

fixSteps.title: Centre pan
fixSteps.instruction: Place cookware centred on the zone, at least the minimum diameter marked.

videoSearchQuery: Electrolux cooktop E3 pan not detected

faq.a: Only if a magnet does not stick firmly to the pan base.

title: Supply Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Mains voltage is too high or too low for safe induction operation.
fullDescription:
The generator monitors supply voltage and trips to E4 when it falls outside roughly 195-253 V AC. The cooktop disables all zones until normal voltage returns.

This is frequently a site wiring issue, a loose neutral, or a failed breaker rather than a cooktop fault.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician measure line-to-neutral voltage at the cooktop terminal.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the appliance is wired per the diagram on the terminal cover.

whenToCallPro: Always - mains voltage diagnosis requires a licensed electrician.

faq.a: No, cooktops draw far more than a UPS can support; fix the supply instead.

title: Overvoltage Protection
shortDescription: Supply voltage has exceeded the upper safety threshold.
fullDescription:
E5 is raised when the generator sees a sustained overvoltage, typically above 253 V. This protects the IGBTs and capacitors in the induction module.

Frequent causes are utility swells, a lost neutral, or improper 3-phase wiring that places the appliance across two lines instead of line-neutral.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker immediately to protect the appliance.

fixSteps.title: Electrician diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Have the supply checked and corrected before reconnecting.

whenToCallPro: Always - overvoltage can damage many appliances and is a safety hazard.

faq.a: Possibly - after the supply is corrected, watch for further fault codes.

title: Zone Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: A glass-top NTC sensor for a cooking zone reads out of range.
fullDescription:
Each zone has an NTC sensor pressed against the glass to monitor temperature. E6 means one of those sensors is shorted or open.

Replacement usually requires removing the cooktop and swapping the affected sensor harness at the generator board.

fixSteps.title: Identify zone
fixSteps.instruction: Note which zone displays E6; only that sensor needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooktop, unclip the NTC from the glass, and fit a new one.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable removing the cooktop and working near mains terminals.

faq.q: Can one bad sensor disable all zones?
faq.a: Usually only the affected zone, but some models lock out the whole cooktop.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
shortDescription: The cooktop cooling fan is not running at the expected speed.
fullDescription:
The generator uses a tacho-feedback fan to cool the IGBTs. E7 is posted when the tacho signal is missing or too slow, suggesting a failing fan bearing, obstructed impeller, or broken harness.

Continued operation with poor cooling will trigger E2 and eventually damage the power module.
symptoms: Loud fan or no fan sound

fixSteps.title: Access fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooktop and locate fan on the generator module.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clear debris; replace if fan still does not spin freely.

whenToCallPro: If the fan is fine, the tacho circuit on the board needs pro diagnosis.

faq.a: No, running without cooling will damage the generator.

title: Touch Control Short Circuit
shortDescription: A touch key is permanently detected as pressed.
fullDescription:
The capacitive touch controller sees a key as active for longer than the allowed time, typically 10 seconds, and raises E8. Water, spilled food, or a cracked glass over the sensor area are the usual culprits.

Clean and dry the surface thoroughly; if that fails, the control board is suspect.

causes.cause: Liquid or food on touch area

fixSteps.title: Clean glass
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe touch area dry with a soft microfibre cloth.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If E8 returns, replace the touch control PCB.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not help and you are not confident replacing boards.

faq.q: Can I still use the cooktop?
faq.a: No, the safety lockout disables all zones until E8 clears.

title: Generator Internal Fault
shortDescription: The induction power module reports an internal error.
fullDescription:
E9 is a catch-all for internal generator faults such as IGBT over-current, resonant circuit failure, or self-test errors at power-up. It generally indicates the generator board has failed and needs replacement.

Before replacing, verify supply voltage, fan operation, and cookware compatibility to rule out secondary causes.

fixSteps.title: Reset power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn breaker off for 10 minutes; restore and test.

fixSteps.title: Replace generator
fixSteps.instruction: If E9 persists, have a technician replace the induction generator.

whenToCallPro: Yes - generator work involves high-voltage capacitors and should be done by a technician.

faq.a: For mid-range and premium models, yes; on older units weigh cost against replacement.

title: Configuration or EEPROM Error
shortDescription: The cooktop has lost its stored configuration data.
fullDescription:
E10 signals that the control board cannot read or write its EEPROM, so the cooktop does not know its model configuration and refuses to operate.

A service-menu reconfiguration sometimes works; otherwise the control board must be replaced with one that has the correct model image.

fixSteps.title: Service reset
fixSteps.instruction: Technician enters service mode and reloads configuration for the model.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: If reload fails, replace the touch control board.

whenToCallPro: Always - requires service-menu access only available to authorised technicians.

faq.q: Will a factory reset fix this?
faq.a: Only a service-mode configuration reload works; user resets do not clear E10.
